Partial failure rolls bytes back; a superseded bundle still under active/ is resumed by the same verb.

Measured honesty gap this verb must not reproduce. F86: across ledger-bearing archives the run-ledger ends at the archive gate Decision; the folklore applied writes and the move leave no machine record, so the ledger cannot show that the transition it gates ever happened. F86.1 confirmed that on a close that actually ran. Supersede is the same folklore shape and was unrecorded. A verb that writes status and moves and still appends nothing to Decisions looks like that gap; whether it is that gap is a decision below, not an inheritance. F115: the brief's equivalence was wrong. F86's gap is a gate Decision standing in for work the gate did not do. There is no supersede gate. The residual, once the lint-checked status plus Replacement exist, is that the record is a state, not an event: it carries no time, actor, or evidence that the verb ran.

Goals.Goal: A new top-level ngrace root named supersede, defined in src/grace-supersede.ts, registered in src/grace.ts alongside the existing roots by a static import of that module, branded with defineGraceCommand so BOOLEAN_SPACE_GUARD_BRAND holds, listed in liveCommandRoots, and present as an ngrace supersede token in a README.md CLI Overview table row. It is not a gate subcommand and not a spec or plan subcommand. It is not an extra root exported from src/grace-generate.ts.

That verb is the sanctioned superseded close. Given argv token change (the active bundle being abandoned) and argv token replacement (a different C-*), and after validation, it surgically sets the spec root status to superseded, does the same to plan.xml when that file exists, writes a Replacement element naming the replacement on each artifact that does not already name it, and renameSyncs the bundle directory from active/ to archive/. Companions (design-context.xml, run-ledger.xml, run.xml, run/) move with the directory. It does not fold, does not require no-open-epoch, and does not run gate archive.

The replacement directory must already exist under active/ or archive/. The verb refuses when it does not. It does not call renderChangeSpec, writeSpecNew, or otherwise create the replacement bundle. spec new remains the creator. Atomically with the replacement means the status writes, the Replacement element, and the move are one verb that names an already-existing successor, not that the successor is minted.

Failure is fail-closed and resumable. Validate before any write. Write the artifact bytes, then renameSync the directory. On any failure after the first artifact write, restore the original file bytes while the directory is still under active/ and exit nonzero. A process crash that leaves status superseded under active/ with the requested replacement is completed by re-running the same verb (skip matching writes, do the move). Do not introduce rmSync or unlinkSync of the bundle directory.

Skill text this bundle owns teaches that path: ngrace-plan approved_plan_immutability names the verb, the replacement-first order, and the named checks; ngrace-execute preflight and durable-state-changed name the verb instead of folklore supersede and replan; ngrace-explainer references/contract-driven-dev.md names the verb. Decided here: ordering and recovery. 1. Validate, write nothing: change id well-formed; replacement id well-formed and different; source is a directory under active/ and not under archive/; dest archive/C-* does not already exist; replacement is a directory under active/ or archive/; spec.xml exists; root status on spec (and plan if present) is draft or approved, or the resume case below; opening-tag status is locatable as either quote style on the status attribute (F114). 2. On throw after step 3, writeFileSync the original bytes back onto any file this invocation already changed (still under active/ because the rename did not happen) and exit nonzero. Do not serializeGraceXmlDocument the spec or plan. EXDEV on renameSync is refuse after that rollback; this bundle does not implement copy-then-delete (that path needs rmSync and would break the A15.1 pin). Resume: source under active/, spec (and plan if present) already superseded and naming exactly the requested replacement; skip matching writes; do the rename. Already in archive as superseded with that replacement: refuse, already done, nonzero. Applied, rejected, or cancelled: refuse even in active/. Existing replacement set nonempty and not exactly the requested id: refuse. Spec without plan: write spec only; do not invent a plan (C-LEDGER-READ-ABSENCE shape).
